 Common Judgment

These two claim petitions are filed under Sec.166
 Motor Vehicles Act 1989 seeking compensation for the
 for the injuries sustained by the petitioners in a road
 traffic accident.
2.  Both petitions state that on 22-10-2022
about 10.30
a.m. , petitioner in MVC.7207/2022 was  SCCH.13 3 MVC.7206 & 7207/2022  the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-09-HL-9759  while petitioner in MVC.7206/2022 was the pillion  rider.

When they reached near BM hospital, Hunsur  Mysore Road, Mysore, at that time, the driver of a  KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-09-F-4967 (hereinafter  called as offending vehicle), drove the same with high  speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed  against the motorcycle.
As a result, both rider and  pillion rider fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, injured were taken to  Brindavan hospital, Mysore, wherein the pillion rider  was treated as inpatient and underwent surgery and  the rider was treated as outpatient.

3. Petitioner in MVC.7206/2022 has stated that  prior to the accident she was hale and healthy aged  about 52 years and was working as a tailor and  earning 15,000/- per month and due to the  accidental injuries, she suffered permanent disability  and suffered loss of income and earning capacity.
She  has sought for compensation of 10,00,000/- for  injuries sustained by her from the Respondents.

4. Petitioner in MVC.7207/2022 has stated that  prior to the accident he was hale and healthy aged  SCCH.13 4 MVC.7206 & 7207/2022  about 60 years and was doing real estate business and  earning Rs.15,000/-p.m. and due to the accidental  injuries, he suffered permanent disability and suffered  loss of income and earning capacity.

He has sought for  compensation of 2,00,000/- for injuries sustained by Nirupama .B.C vs Ksrtc on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45152118/
2  him from the Respondent.
5. In response to the petition notice, the  Respondent -KSRTC has appeared before the court  through his counsel and filed the written statement in  both the petitions.
During the pendency of Petition, the  respondent no 2 and 3 were impleaded.
They appeared  through their counsel.
Respondent no 2 has resisted  the petition.
The respondent no 3 has filed his  separate written statement.
6. The Respondent - KSRTC in his objections

denied the negligence of its driver and involvement of  the offending bus in the alleged accident inter alia  contending that the offending bus was in its schedule  trip from Vijayanagara Depot, Mysore Division towards  City bus station, Mysore, when it was proceeding  slowly and carefully on the alleged incident place, at  that time, the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-09-  HL-9759 along with pillion rider, ridden the same  SCCH.13 5 MVC.7206 & 7207/2022  without wearing helmet, DL, FC, RC and insurance  policy, rubbed with another two-wheeler and fell down
and sustained injuries.

The another unknown two-  wheeler fled from the spot and the driver of KSRTC  bus after hearing the sound and alighted from the bus,
 observed this incident.
In this regard, driver of KSRTC  bus has given complaint before the concerned police .
Two eyewitnesses namely Savitha and Suryanarayana  gowda, were identified in connection with the incident.
It is further submitted that the KSRTC bus was  involved in the accident and petitioners filed a false  complaint against this respondent.

It has further  denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioners,
 treatment taken by them, disability suffered by them  and also the expenses claimed by the Petitioners.
The  compensation claimed by the Petitioners is exorbitant  without any basis.
On these grounds, the Respondent  prays for dismissal of the petitions.
7. In MVC.7206/2022 the Respondent No.3 - in  its objection statement has admitted the issuance of  policy in respect of offending vehicle.
However, if it is  proved, then its liability is subject to terms and  conditions mentioned in the policy.
It has contended  SCCH.13 6 MVC.7206 & 7207/2022  that the owner of the offending vehicle and the  concerned police have not complied the mandatory  provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.

It has Nirupama .B.C vs Ksrtc on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45152118/
3  denied the negligence on the part of rider of insured  vehicle i.e., motorcycle.
Further it has contended that  the accident has occurred due to negligent driving of  the driver of offending bus and concerned police have  filed charge sheet against the driver of KSRTC bus.
It  has contended that the compensation claimed is highly  excessive.
It has denied the age, avocation and income  of the petitioner as well as deceased, relationship of  Petitioners with the deceased and their dependency  and prayed for dismissal of the petitions.

8. On the basis of above pleadings, the following  issues have been framed :-
 IN MVC.7206/2022

1 . Whether the Petitioner proves that she  sustained injuries when she was a  pillion rider in motorcycle bearing  No.KA-09-HL-9759 on 22-10-2022  about 10.30 a.m., near B.M.hospital,
 Hunsur-Mysore road, Mysore District,
 only due to rash and negligent driving  of the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing  No.KA-09-F-4967?
SCCH.13 7 MVC.7206 & 7207/2022  2.What compensation Petitioner is  entitled?
3. What order?

Additional Issue:
 1. Whether the respondent proves that  the KSRTC Bus bearing No.KA-09-F-  4967 not involved in the accident and  it is falsely implicated and the  respondent is not liable to pay any  compensation?

Whether the Petitioner proves that he  sustained injuries when he was riding  in his motorcycle bearing No.KA-09-  HL-9759 on 22-10-2022 about 10.30  a.m., near B.M.hospital, Hunsur-  Mysore road, Mysore District, only due  to rash and negligent driving of the  driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing  No.KA-09-F-4967?
 2.

What compensation Petitioner is Nirupama .B.C vs Ksrtc on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45152118/
4  entitled?
 3.
What order?
9. As both the petitions arise out of the same  accident, on the application made by the parties, both  the petitions were clubbed and the common evidence  was recorded.
10. In order to substantiate the claim, the injured  Petitioners are examined as PW.1 and 2.

Further,
 doctor and Medical rec ord officer at Brindavan  hospital are examined as PW-3 and 4 and got marked  the documents at Ex.P.1 to 28.
 11.

The driver of KSRTC bus is examined as  RW-1 Respondent No.3 has examined its official as  RW-2 and no documents are got marked.
 12.
I have heard the counsel on both sides and  have perused the material on record.

On the basis of evidence and material  available on record and by considering the facts

, I have  answered the above issues in both the petitions as  under:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.

 for the following:
REASONS  15.
Issue No.1 in both petitions:-

Petitioners  say that on 22-10-2022 about 10.30 a.m., PW-2/
 petitioner in MVC.7207/2022 was the rider of  motorcycle bearing No.KA-09-HL-9759 and PW-1/
 SCCH.13 10 MVC.7206 & 7207/2022  petitioner in MVC.7206/2022 was the pillion rider.
 when they were reached near BM hospital, Hunsur  Mysore Road, Mysore, at that time, the driver of a  KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-09-F-4967, drove the same  with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and  dashed against the motorcycle.
As a result, both rider  and pillion rider fell down and sustained grievous  injuries.
16. PW-2 had gave first information statement to  the police as per Ex.P2.
On the basis of the first  information statement, FIR was registered as Ex.P1.
He  has produced spot mahazar and spot sketch at Ex.P.3  and 4, IMV report at Ex-P-5, wound certificate at  Ex.P.6.
Charge sheet at EX P7 and wound certificate of  PW-2 at EX.P.14.
Wound certificate of injured  petitioner/ PW-1 shows that she has sustained  avulsion fracture medial epicondyle right elbow and  degloving injury right arm + elbow.

Wound certificate  of injured petitioner/ PW-2 shows that he has  sustained multiple superficial, small, tender gazed  abrasions, tenderness over right elbow region, small,
 tender, superficial gazed abrasion injury on right  dorsal outer aspect of forehead.
 SCCH.13 11 MVC.7206 & 7207/2022  17.

It is contention of the respondent no 1 that  the offending KSRTC Bus was not involved in the  alleged accident and there was no rash and negligent  act on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The accident occurred between the offending two  wheeler and petitioners' two wheeler.

The offending  KSRTC Bus was falsely implicated, in order to get Nirupama .B.C vs Ksrtc on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45152118/
6  compensation.
Thereby this respondent is not liable to  pay any compensation to the petitioners.

The police  documents show that the accident occurred due to  negligence on the part of the driver of the offending  KSRTC bus and offending KSRTC Bus involved in the  accident.
 18.

It is contention of the Respondent no 3 that  the accident occurred due to sole negligence of the  driver of the offending KSRTC Bus and there was  negligence on the part of the rider of the offending two  wheeler.
19. The Learned counsel for the Respondent no 1  intensively cross examined the PW1, PW2 and RW2.
It  was suggested that the offending motorcycle was came  from the opposite direction and dashed against the  petitioners' motorcycle, as a result, they fell down.
The  SCCH.13 12 MVC.7206 & 7207/2022  offending motorcycle rider ran away from the spot, in  order to get compensation, wrongly implicated the  offending KSRTC bus.
The Offending KSRTC Bus was  not involved in the accident.
The same was denied.
Further they denied that the entire incident was  captured in CCTV camera.

They expressed their  ignorance as to whether the driver of the offending  bus had submitted the written complaint to the police,
 supported by the signature of two eyewitnesses.

20. Keeping in view of the material available on  record, let us discuss, whether the accident occurred  due to the rash or negligent driving by the driver of the  offending KSRTC bus or due to collision between  offending motorcycle and petitioners' motorcycle.
The  police records show that due to rash and negligent  driving of the offending KSRTC bus the accident  occurred.
As a result, Petitioners sustained grievous  injuries.
21. The Respondent no 1 has set up a specific  plea of non involvement of offending KSRTC Bus in the  accident but has not established the same.

If the  Respondent no 1 had suspected false implication,
 appropriate steps could have been taken by filing

a  SCCH.13 13 MVC.7206 & 7207/2022  complaint before higher authority or seeking the court  ordered investigation into the alleged wrongful  involvement of the vehicle, including examination of  two eye witnesses namely Savitha and Suryanaryana,
Nirupama .B.C vs Ksrtc on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45152118/
7  and by producing the footage of CCTV Camera.
There  is no claim for the respondent no 1 that the police  officer was in collusion.
The investigation conducted by  the police culminated in a charge sheet being filed.
The respondent no 1 has not produced credible  evidence to prove that the offending KSRTC bus was  not involved in the accident.
It is not established that  the offending two vehicle came from opposite side and  dashed against the victims' two wheeler.
A mere  allegation that the offending two wheeler caused the  accident and not the offending KSRTC bus, the  offending KSRTC bus was falsely implicated are not  sufficient.
Such an allegation must be substantiated  with cogent evidence.
22. There are no materials on record to disprove  the PW-1 and PW2 evidence and to prove the  contention of the Respondent no 1.
The evidence of  PW-1 and PW2 corroborated with the documents  produced.
There is nothing elicited to disprove the case  SCCH.13 14 MVC.7206 & 7207/2022  of the petitioners.
It is well settled principle that Motor  Vehicles Act is beneficial legislation, the tribunal need  not to go for the strict proof of rash and negligence.
Charge sheet prima-facie establishes the rash and  negligence on the part of the driver of the offending  KSRTC bus.
From all the above materials clearly  indicate that the accident was due to the negligence of  driver of offending KSRTC Bus.
Based on the entire  records, I hold that the driver of offending KSRTC Bus  was negligent in causing the accident due to which  the petitioners sustained injuries in the RTA.

Hence,
 this issue is answered in the Affirmative.
23. Issue No.2 in MVC.7206/2022:
The  Petitioner has lead cogent evidence and have proved  that the accident has occurred due to the rash or  negligent driving of offending vehicle.

Hence,
 Respondent being the owner of the offending bus is  liable to pay the above compensation.
Hence, I answer  issue no.2 in the negative.
24. Issue No.3 in MVC.7206/2022:
The  Petitioner states that due to the accident she has  sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately she was taken  to Brindavan hospital, Mysore, wherein she has taken  SCCH.13 15 MVC.7206 & 7207/2022  treatment as an inpatient and underwent surgery and  discharged with an advice to take complete bed rest Nirupama .B.C vs Ksrtc on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45152118/
8  and to continue further follow up treatment.
She has  stated that at the time of accident, she was working as  a tailor and was earning .20,000/- p.m.
Due to the  accidental injuries she is unable to do her work and  continue as earlier and suffered loss of income.
She  has lost her normal life as earlier and suffering huge  loss of income.
She is facing difficulties in her day-  today activities.

PW-4 MRO at Brindavan hospital,
 Mysore has produced the documents at Ex.P.23 to 26.
 25.

PW-3 Dr.Nagaraj B.N. Orthopedic surgeon, at  Sai Ortho and Dentral Center, Bengaluru, has deposed  that the Petitioner has sustained right elbow medial  condyle fracture in a RTA occurred on 22-10-2022  and he has stated that she has underwent surgery at  Brindavan hospital inserted ORIF with CC screw.

PW-2  has examined the Petitioner clinically and  radiologically while assessing disability and note of the  following complaints: weakness in the right elbow,
 inability to fold or extend elbow.
As a result she is  unable to carry her avocation as earlier.
He has  assessed the total disability of right arm at 30% and  SCCH.13 16 MVC.7206 & 7207/2022  whole body disability at 10%.

PW-3/ doctor has  produced clinical notes and X-ray at Ex.P-20 and 21.
 26.
By the evidence of the Petitioner and the  cross-examination of PW-3/doctor nothing has been  elicited to disbelieve his version.
It is clear that the  petitioner has sustained right elbow medial condyle  fracture.
On careful reading of testimonies of PW1  and PW2 , it appears that the petitioner is facing  difficulty to do her daily activities.
Doctor has deposed  that total disability of right arm at 30% and whole  body disability at 10%.
However, the doctor has  assessed only physical disability and not functional  disability.
Therefore, considering the difficulties and  evidence of PW-3 and also by considering the age of the  Petitioner and avocation, the functional disability is  assessed at 10%.
27. The Petitioner has stated that she was aged  about 52 years, in support of her age she has produced  her Aadhar card at Ex.P.10, which shows her date of  birth as 26-08-1969.
Therefore, as on date of accident  her age is considered as 53 years.

Therefore, the  proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is 11.
 SCCH.13 17 MVC.7206 & 7207/2022  28.

The Petitioner has claimed that she was Nirupama .B.C vs Ksrtc on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45152118/
9  working as a tailor and was earning .20,000/- p.m.
To prove her avocation and income she has not  produced any supportive documents.

In the absence of  sufficient materials to prove the petitioner's income , it  would be reasonable to take the notional income of the  Petitioner as .15,500/-p.m.
 29.

Thus this tribunal is of the opinion that the  petitioner who sustained the injuries is entitled for  compensation under the following heads:
 30. Loss of future income on account of  permanent disability:
Looking into the nature of  injury, it definitely affects the working capacity of any  person.
the considering nature of injury, avocation  and doctor's evidence the total functional disability of  the Petitioner is considered at 10%.
Thus, loss of  future income
31. Pain and sufferings:

So far as the  compensation under non-pecuniary damages are  concerned, considering the fact that the Petitioner has  suffered grievous injuries and treated as an inpatient  SCCH.13 18 MVC.7206 & 7207/2022  which caused her immeasurable mental agony and  pain

, I am of the opinion that an amount of  .35,000/- would be just and fair compensation under  the head pain and sufferings.
 32. Loss of amenities of life:
For loss of  amenities of life undoubtedly Petitioner is sure to  suffer in her day today activities and face hardships.

Hence, Petitioner is awarded .25,000/- for Loss of  amenities of life, frustration, disappointment,
 unhappiness and inconvenience etc.
 33.
Medical expenses:

Under the pecuniary  damages, expenses relating to treatment,
 hospitalization and medicines, the Petitioner has  relied on medical bills for .1,32,905/- at Ex.P.9.
Though counsel for Respondent has cross-examined  the PW-1, nothing has been elicited to disprove the  medical bills.
The medical bills appears to be genuine.
Hence, Petitioner is awarded .1,32,905 /- towards  Medical Expenses.
34. Future medical expenses: PW-3 Doctor has  stated that Petitioner needs surgery for removal of  implants which cost around Rs.30,000/-.

But he has  SCCH.13 19 MVC.7206 & 7207/2022 Nirupama .B.C vs Ksrtc on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45152118/
10  not produced any estimation report.
In the absence of  clear evidence, it is just and reasonable to award  .15,000/- towards future medical expenses.

35. Conveyance, food, nourishment and  attendant charges: Ex.P.8 - Discharge summary  shows that, petitioner was treated as an inpatient at  Brindavan hospital, Mysore, from 22-10-2022 to 27-  10-2022 i.e., for a period of 6 days.

Therefore, it is just  and reasonable to award compensation of .10,000/-
 under the head of conveyance, food, nourishment  and attendant charges.
 36. Loss of earning during laid up period:

With  regard to loss of earnings during treatment,
 considering 6 days admission in the hospital as  inpatient and around 2 months for rest is considered  and loss of earnings during treatment is calculated for  2 months.
As the monthly income of the Petitioner is  already considered as .15,500/- per month, loss of  earning during laid up period

Moreover, it is also not proved that due to the  accidental injuries he is suffering from difficulties and  is unable to work as earlier.

Considering the  nature of injury, treatment taken by Petitioner, his age  and the date of accident I deem it proper to award  40,000/- of global compensation under all the  conventional heads, as the Petitioner has suffered  some sort of pain and had to take treatment for his  injuries.
39. Liability:
As already discussed above in Issue  No.1 that the accident has occurred due to the  negligence of driver of KSRTC Bus.
Therefore, the  Respondent No.1 being the owner and insurer of  KSRTC Bus is liable to pay the above compensation to  the Petitioners with interest at 6% p.a.
Petition against  SCCH.13 22 MVC.7206 & 7207/2022  the respondent No.2 and 3 in MVC.7206/2022 is  dismissed.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The accident occurred between the offending two  wheeler and petitioners' two wheeler.
It is contention of the Respondent no 3 that  the accident occurred due to sole negligence of the  driver of the offending KSRTC Bus and there was  negligence on the part of the rider of the offending two  wheeler.
The Offending KSRTC Bus was  not involved in the accident.
The  police records show that due to rash and negligent  driving of the offending KSRTC bus the accident  occurred.
As a result, Petitioners sustained grievous  injuries.
21. The Respondent no 1 has set up a specific  plea of non involvement of offending KSRTC Bus in the  accident but has not established the same.
If the  Respondent no 1 had suspected false implication,
 appropriate steps could have been taken by filing
a  SCCH.13 13 MVC.7206 & 7207/2022  complaint before higher authority or seeking the court  ordered investigation into the alleged wrongful  involvement of the vehicle, including examination of  two eye witnesses namely Savitha and Suryanaryana,
Nirupama .B.C vs Ksrtc on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45152118/
7  and by producing the footage of CCTV Camera.
There  is no claim for the respondent no 1 that the police  officer was in collusion.
The investigation conducted by  the police culminated in a charge sheet being filed.
The respondent no 1 has not produced credible  evidence to prove that the offending KSRTC bus was  not involved in the accident.
It is not established that  the offending two vehicle came from opposite side and  dashed against the victims' two wheeler.
A mere  allegation that the offending two wheeler caused the  accident and not the offending KSRTC bus, the  offending KSRTC bus was falsely implicated are not  sufficient.
Such an allegation must be substantiated  with cogent evidence.
22. There are no materials on record to disprove  the PW-1 and PW2 evidence and to prove the  contention of the Respondent no 1.
The evidence of  PW-1 and PW2 corroborated with the documents  produced.
There is nothing elicited to disprove the case  SCCH.13 14 MVC.7206 & 7207/2022  of the petitioners.
It is well settled principle that Motor  Vehicles Act is beneficial legislation, the tribunal need  not to go for the strict proof of rash and negligence.
From all the above materials clearly  indicate that the accident was due to the negligence of  driver of offending KSRTC Bus.
To prove her avocation and income she has not  produced any supportive documents.

p.a. from the date of petition till the realisation.
Respondent No.1 shall deposit the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of compensation amount in MVC.7206/2022, 25% of the amount shall be kept in FD in the name of petitioner in any Nationalised or Scheduled Bank of her choice for a period of 2 years and balance 75% shall be disbursed to the petitioner through E- payment on proper identification.
After deposit of amount in MVC.7207/2022, entire amount with interest shall be disbursed to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,000/- each.
Draw award accordingly.
